title: JDK, Compilation, and Program Structure
summary: Set up a Java development workflow and understand source files, classes, the main method, compilation, bytecode, and actionable compiler diagnostics.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply the Java behavior taught in JDK, Compilation, and Program Structure
Compile, run, and test the behavior with observable evidence
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: The JDK provides the compiler and runtime tools. `javac Main.java` checks source and emits bytecode in `Main.class`; `java Main` starts the JVM and invokes `public static void main(String[] args)`. A public class name must match its source filename. Java is statically typed, so many invalid operations are rejected before execution. Read the first relevant compiler diagnostic, correct one cause at a time, and recompile. Packages organize names and should match directory structure in normal projects. Do not edit generated `.class` files or commit them as source.
keyPoints: The JDK provides the compiler and runtime tools.
commonMistakes: a JRE-only installation may not provide javac
editing a class file is not a source workflow

sections.heading: Guided practice
sections.content:
1. Save the example in the matching source file.
2. Predict compiler and runtime results.
3. Compile with javac.
4. Correct diagnostics one cause at a time.
5. Run with java.
6. Add an assertion for the intended behavior.
